questions.topic: Patient safety, product quality, data integrity
questions.question: GAMP 5 repeatedly uses the phrase "patient safety, product quality, and data integrity". What is its main purpose?

options.A: To indicate that the Guide focuses only on the physical attributes of the product, such as appearance, content, and packaging integrity, with data-related issues handled separately
options.B: To emphasize that patient safety is affected by the integrity of critical records, data, and decisions, and not only by the physical attributes of the product
options.C: To indicate that each of the three corresponds to a separate regulatory document that must be written independently, with none omitted and each separately approved
options.D: To indicate that only suppliers must meet all three requirements, while regulated companies need to focus only on patient safety

questions.explanation: §1.3 states that patient safety is affected by the integrity of critical records, data, and decisions as well as by the physical attributes of the product, which is why the three are listed together. The statement that narrows the scope to physical attributes is the opposite of the original text.

questions.question: According to GAMP 5, life cycle activities should be scaled according to which set of factors?

options.A: System purchase cost, number of users, and supplier company size, with larger values meaning leaner, simpler activities
options.B: Quality department headcount, number of existing SOPs, and audit frequency, with larger values meaning leaner, simpler documentation
options.C: System go-live date, project budget, and supplier country, with the depth and breadth of activities set by contract terms
options.D: Impact on patient safety and similar concerns, system complexity and novelty, and the outcome of supplier assessment

questions.explanation: §2.1.3 lists three scaling bases: the impact from risk assessment, system complexity and novelty, and the results of supplier assessment; business impact may also play a part. Purchase cost and the like are not factors listed in the original text.

questions.question: A regulated company plans to use a supplier's existing test documentation to avoid duplicating work. According to GAMP 5, where should the justification for using this documentation come from?

options.A: A satisfactory supplier assessment, which may include a supplier audit
options.B: The supplier's verbal assurances and the price agreed in the contract; once both parties sign, it is considered sufficient
options.C: The supplier holding any quality certification, which automatically exempts the regulated company from all verification and review work
options.D: The format and structure of the supplier's documents matching the regulated company's SOPs exactly, otherwise they may never be used

questions.explanation: §2.1.5 states that the justification for using supplier documentation is provided by a satisfactory supplier assessment, and the documents must still be evaluated for suitability, correctness, and completeness. The statement that format and structure must match SOPs exactly is the opposite of the original text, which calls for flexibility regarding format and structure.

questions.question: For systems that control or monitor CPPs (critical process parameters), how does GAMP 5 §2.1.4 expect these CPPs to be traced?

options.A: To the supplier's outgoing inspection specifications, and then to the delivery time and price terms in the purchase contract
options.B: To the equipment operators' training records, and then to the list of findings from the annual internal audit
options.C: To the CQAs, and ultimately to the QTPP and the related regulatory filing
options.D: To the system's IT infrastructure architecture diagram, and then to the data backup and restore schedule settings

questions.explanation: §2.1.4 requires that CPPs be traceable to CQAs and ultimately back to the QTPP and regulatory filings, so that risk decisions rest on science and process understanding. The traceability targets in the other options are unrelated to the original text.

questions.question: A pharmaceutical company's internal IT team provides support and maintenance for production line systems. According to GAMP 5 §1.3's description of a supplier, how should this internal team be regarded?

options.A: Not a supplier, because a supplier means only an external vendor outside the company with a purchase contract
options.B: A supplier, because supplier includes IT service and IT support service providers, whether internal or external
options.C: A regulator, because the internal team is responsible for overseeing whether the regulated company complies with regulatory requirements
options.D: The Quality Unit, because any team providing system support must be independent of the production department

questions.explanation: §1.3 explains that supplier includes providers of software, hardware, equipment, system integration, IT services, and IT support services, whether internal or external. The statement that a supplier means only an external vendor and excludes internal teams does not match the original text.

questions.question: According to GAMP 5 §3.1, by when at the latest should the GxP assessment that determines whether a system is GxP be completed?

options.A: By the start of the project phase at the latest, as part of the initial system risk assessment (Step 1)
options.B: At the first periodic review in the operation phase, assessed together with it
options.C: After the validation report is complete and approved by the quality unit, going back to perform and record the assessment
options.D: In the week the system finishes testing and is prepared for go-live, completed and signed together with the go-live approval documents, and confirmed by the quality unit

questions.explanation: §3.1 requires GxP regulated systems to be identified before the start of the project phase, as part of the initial risk assessment. If the assessment is delayed until after validation, it cannot influence requirements and supplier selection.

questions.question: According to GAMP 5 §3.1, what are the four main phases of the computerized system life cycle?

options.A: Planning, Specification, Testing, Release, with the life cycle complete at go-live release
options.B: Concept, Design, Verification, Release, with the system no longer part of the life cycle after go-live
options.C: Concept, Project, Operation, Retirement, covering all activities from initial concept to system retirement
options.D: Initiation, Project, Operation, Archiving, with data archiving as the end point of the whole life cycle

questions.explanation: §3.1 states that the life cycle covers all activities from initial concept to retirement, and the four phases are Concept, Project, Operation, and Retirement. The statement that excludes the operation phase from the life cycle does not match the original text.

questions.question: An automated manufacturing equipment item contains a computer system. According to GAMP 5 §3.3, how should the computer system of this type of equipment be handled?

options.A: After equipment commissioning, arrange a separate, full computer system validation, performed by an independent team
options.B: Leave it entirely to the supplier, with the regulated company retaining no specification or verification documents
options.C: Replace all specification and verification activities with routine operating SOPs, to save validation time and cost
options.D: Avoid separate computer system validation, and fold specification and verification into the integrated engineering approach for the equipment as a whole

questions.explanation: §3.3 states that automated manufacturing equipment should avoid separate computer system validation, and specification and verification should be part of the integrated engineering approach. Arranging a separate full validation after equipment commissioning is exactly the duplicate validation the original text seeks to avoid.

questions.question: A company purchases an automated test tool for use in system verification. According to GAMP 5 §4.2.3, what is required of such test tools?

options.A: Full IQ/OQ/PQ validation must be performed, and repeated in full after every version update
options.B: They need a documented assessment of adequacy and must be controlled in use, but do not need to be validated
options.C: No assessment or control is needed, because the tool itself is not part of the system and therefore does not need to be managed
options.D: A supplier's shipping certificate is enough, and the user need not establish any control or usage rules

questions.explanation: §4.2.3 cites EU Annex 11 Clause 4.7: test tools need a documented assessment of adequacy and must be controlled, but validation is not required. Requiring full IQ/OQ/PQ validation goes beyond the original text.

questions.question: After a system has completed withdrawal, the company wants to destroy its data and documents. According to GAMP 5 §4.4.3, when may disposal take place?

options.A: As soon as the system is decommissioned, with the IT department deciding on its own to destroy the data immediately
options.B: At any stage, as long as the quality unit agrees verbally, with no documented record needed
options.C: Data may first be migrated to any media, after which the data in the original system can be deleted at any time regardless of retention periods
options.D: Only after the data and documents have reached the period set by the company's records retention policy, and following an authorized and documented procedure

questions.explanation: §4.4.3 states that data and documents must not be disposed of before the records retention period is reached, and disposal must follow an authorized and documented procedure. Letting the IT department decide on its own after decommissioning looks only at the system status and ignores the retention period.

questions.question: GAMP 5 §5.3 cites the two main QRM principles of ICH Q9. Which of the following is correct?

options.A: Risk evaluation should rely solely on the number of historical defects; all projects should invest the same level of documentation in QRM
options.B: Risk evaluation should be led by the supplier; the formality of QRM depends only on project budget and schedule pressure
options.C: Risk evaluation should be done solely by the IT department; QRM documentation need only be completed in one go when the system is retired
options.D: Risk evaluation should be based on scientific knowledge and linked to patient protection; the effort and documentation of QRM must be commensurate with the level of risk

questions.explanation: §5.3 cites ICH Q9: risk evaluation is based on scientific knowledge and linked to patient protection, and the effort, formality, and documentation of QRM must be commensurate with risk. The statement that all projects should have the same level of documentation violates the commensurate principle.

questions.question: A LIMS supports a regulated process and holds regulated data, with the IT department acting as system owner. According to GAMP 5 §6.2.3.2, who owns this data?

options.A: The system owner, because it is responsible for system availability, support and maintenance, and data security
options.B: The supplier, because the system was developed by the supplier and the data is stored on a platform provided by the supplier
options.C: The GxP process owner, not the system owner
options.D: The quality unit, because all GxP data is held and managed solely by the quality unit under regulation

questions.explanation: §6.2.3.2 states that for a system that supports a regulated process and holds regulated data, data ownership rests with the GxP process owner, not the system owner. The system owner is responsible for availability, support, and data security, and is easily mistaken for the data owner.

questions.question: A company buys off-the-shelf software (Category 3) that can be used without configuration, with only factory parameter ranges to choose from. According to GAMP 5 §7.1, what is the interaction between supplier and regulated company usually?

options.A: Usually limited to providing documentation, training, support, and maintenance, with the product itself developed and maintained under good practice
options.B: The supplier usually must assist with specification, configuration, verification, and system operation, equivalent to the involvement for configured products (Category 4)
options.C: The supplier usually must take part in the full project life cycle and provide support during operation, equivalent to custom applications (Category 5)
options.D: The supplier need not follow any good practice, because the product is already on the market and the user is responsible for all quality

questions.explanation: §7.1 explains that for Category 3 standard products, supplier involvement is usually limited to documentation, training, support, and maintenance. The statement that the supplier must assist with specification, configuration, verification, and operation describes Category 4, and the statement that it must take part in the full project life cycle describes Category 5.

questions.question: A company SOP requires a second person to witness every test step, and the tester must sign each step. According to GAMP 5 §8.5.4, how is this practice viewed?

options.A: It is a mandatory regulatory requirement, and must be used for all computerized system testing, otherwise the test results are invalid and not accepted
options.B: Witnessing is not required and step-by-step signatures are disproportionate; some tests (such as FAT/SAT) may be witnessed as needed
options.C: Only Category 5 custom applications are exempt from witnessing; all other categories must be witnessed and signed step by step
options.D: Using an audit trail completely prohibits any form of witnessing, because witnessing affects test results

questions.explanation: §8.5.4 states that test witnessing is not a requirement and adds considerable burden with no added value; requiring step-by-step signatures is disproportionate and unnecessary, though a company may still witness some tests for business, communication, or training reasons. The statement that witnessing is completely prohibited is not from the original text.

questions.question: Testers habitually take an additional screenshot at every test step. According to GAMP 5 §8.5.3, how should this additional secondary evidence be handled?

options.A: A screenshot must accompany every step, otherwise the test is not accepted and reviewers cannot objectively judge the results
options.B: Screenshots may be kept as the primary basis for test results only when the system has an audit trail enabled
options.C: Screenshots should replace the original primary test results or output and become the only test evidence that needs to be retained
options.D: Unnecessary in most cases and adds cost; keep them only where they add value, such as complex results, visual results, or before-and-after comparisons

questions.explanation: §8.5.3 states that additional screenshots beyond the primary results are unnecessary in most cases and should be produced only where valuable, such as for complex results, visual or graphical results, or before-and-after comparisons. The statement that screenshots replace the primary results and become the only evidence contradicts the fact that they are "additional" evidence.

questions.question: According to GAMP 5 Appendix M1 §9.3.2, who usually approves the computerized system validation plan?

options.A: Only the supplier's project manager and software development manager, with the regulated company merely keeping a copy on file
options.B: Only the system owner alone, with the quality unit taking part in review only at the validation report stage
options.C: The process owner and the quality unit, with the meaning of each approval defined in advance
options.D: The regulatory authority, before it can be executed, and the regulated company may not begin any validation activity before approval

questions.explanation: §9.3.2 states that the validation plan is usually approved by the process owner and the quality unit, and the meaning of each approval should be defined. The statement that only the system owner approves, excluding the quality unit from plan approval, does not match the original text.

questions.question: A company adopts a SaaS system for which most specification and verification work is performed by the service provider. According to GAMP 5 §9.3.2, how should the validation plan address this?

options.A: Regulatory responsibility can be delegated to the service provider, so the plan need not describe any validation or verification approach or scope
options.B: Describe how the supplier's specification and verification will be leveraged, and cover configuration, verification, and UAT; regulatory responsibility cannot be delegated
options.C: Require the regulated company to redo all of the supplier's development and testing before the system can be considered fit for its intended use and purpose
options.D: Because SaaS is operated by the supplier, no user acceptance activity is needed, and reports issued by the supplier are taken as final

questions.explanation: §9.3.2 states that the regulated company cannot delegate regulatory responsibility but can leverage the supplier through risk assessment and governance; the plan must describe configuration specification, verification, and UAT. Requiring the company to redo all of the supplier's development and testing is not what the original text requires.

questions.question: A company is assessing the supplier of a low-impact system and the supplier of a high-impact system. According to GAMP 5 Appendix M2 §10.3, what is the principle for choosing the assessment method?

options.A: A basic assessment is usually sufficient for low-impact systems, while high-impact systems may need a formal audit
options.B: Low-impact systems also always require an on-site audit; only for high-impact systems is a questionnaire used instead
options.C: Postal audits are prohibited for any system, because a questionnaire cannot reflect the supplier's actual quality status
options.D: A virtual online audit is a lower-level assessment, with depth that can be lower than an on-site audit

questions.explanation: §10.3 states that a basic assessment is usually sufficient for low-impact systems, while high-impact systems may need a formal audit; a postal audit can be used for suppliers of standard and configured products; a virtual audit is regarded as a subset of an on-site audit, with the same depth. The statement that a virtual online audit may have lower depth is the opposite.

questions.question: According to GAMP 5 Appendix M3 §11.5.3.1, when should the initial risk assessment (Step 1) be performed, and how is it sequenced relative to the RS?

options.A: After PQ is complete, to decide whether previously omitted GxP-related documents need to be added
options.B: After the RS is complete and approved, because the assessment must rely on the finalized, complete requirements
options.C: After the functional risk assessment is complete, as a summary and confirmation of its results
options.D: At or before the start of the project phase, earlier than RS development, and at worst in parallel with it

questions.explanation: §11.5.3.1 states that the initial risk assessment should be performed at or before the start of the project phase, the earlier the better, because this step determines whether the system is within GxP scope and may influence the RS. Placing it after the RS would prevent the results from feeding back into the requirements.

questions.question: A user writes a macro in spreadsheet software using its internal scripting language to meet a specific business need. According to GAMP 5 §12.3.4, how should this custom component be categorized?

options.A: Category 3, because the underlying spreadsheet software is itself a standard commercial off-the-shelf product
options.B: Category 4, because the macro merely adds user-defined configuration to existing software
options.C: Treated as Category 5, because it is a custom software component written or modified to meet a specific business need
options.D: Category 1, because macros are infrastructure software and need no special validation or risk assessment

questions.explanation: §12.3.4 states that custom components developed in an internal scripting language, written or modified to meet specific needs (such as macros), should be treated as Category 5. Treating the macro as mere configuration (Category 4) underestimates the risk.

questions.question: The company is implementing a standard product (Category 3). According to GAMP 5 Appendix M5 §13.3, how is the regulated company's design review of this system usually handled?

options.A: A design review by the regulated company is usually not needed, because it is a standard product
options.B: A full formal design review must always be performed, producing an independent review report for audit
options.C: It can be done only by the quality unit alone, and must be completed and approved before testing begins
options.D: It is performed only at the periodic review after go-live, using the supplier's report as the sole basis

questions.explanation: §13.3 states that for standard products (Category 3) the regulated company usually does not need a design review; the rigor of design review depends on GxP risk, complexity, and novelty. The statement that a full formal design review is always required is inconsistent with the principle of scaling by risk.

questions.question: In a small, low-risk system, the requirements, design, and test documents use the same numbering for the temperature recording function. According to GAMP 5 §13.4.3, how is this practice viewed?

options.A: It applies only to high-risk Category 5 systems; small systems must still build a separate traceability matrix
options.B: It is not accepted; traceability can be achieved only through a separate RTM document
options.C: A manual RTM is more reliable than automated tools, so manual traceability is recommended in preference to tools
options.D: Traceability can be achieved without a separate matrix, suitable for small, low-risk systems, though use of tools is still recommended

questions.explanation: §13.4.3 (Figure 13.1) explains that traceability can be achieved with consistent numbering, which is suitable for small, low-risk situations, though use of tools is still recommended. The statement that a manual RTM is more reliable than tools is the opposite of the original text, which notes that manual methods are hard to maintain and keep correct.

questions.question: According to GAMP 5 Appendix M12 §20.3.3, in a function hierarchy, what is the risk relationship between a subsidiary function and its parent function?

options.A: The risk of a subsidiary function is always higher than its parent, so each must be fully assessed at the highest rigor
options.B: The risk of a subsidiary function will not be higher than its parent, so assessing subsidiary functions under a low-risk parent function yields little or no benefit
options.C: All subsidiary functions, whatever their risk, must be tested and documented at the same level of detail
options.D: Subsidiary and parent functions must have the same risk, so assessing one is enough to represent the whole hierarchy

questions.explanation: §20.3.3 states that the risk of a subsidiary function cannot be higher than that of its parent function, so assessing subsidiary functions of a low-risk parent function offers little or no benefit. The statement that all subsidiary functions use the same level of detail is the opposite of the principle that risk determines the level of testing detail.

questions.question: According to GAMP 5 Appendix M11 §19.2.2, which category does infrastructure software belong to, and what is required?

options.A: Category 3, requiring full validation and version-by-version verification like a standard product
options.B: Category 4, requiring configuration specifications to be completed one by one and each setting independently verified
options.C: GAMP Category 1, and therefore it is qualified rather than validated
options.D: Category 5, requiring a full design review and source code review at the level of custom software

questions.explanation: §19.2.2 states that infrastructure software is GAMP Category 1, so it is qualified rather than validated. Treating it as Category 3 application software requiring full validation is incorrect.

questions.topic: Quality unit role in IT infrastructure
questions.question: According to GAMP 5 Appendix M11 §19.4, what is the appropriate role of the quality unit in IT infrastructure changes?

options.A: It need not be involved in low-impact changes such as firmware updates or adding virus definitions, but may take part in replacing a database engine or a major operating system upgrade
options.B: It must approve every virus definition update and firmware update, so that all infrastructure changes have quality unit sign-off
options.C: It should lead the technical solutions and decisions for infrastructure, because the quality unit understands IT technology and system design best
options.D: No quality oversight is needed at all; the IT department decides everything and need not define an IT quality framework

questions.explanation: §19.4 states that the quality unit need not worry about lower-impact changes such as firmware updates or adding virus definitions, but may take part in replacing a database engine shared by several GxP applications or a major operating system upgrade; it should also not become involved in technical decisions. The statement that no quality oversight is needed at all is the opposite of the original text.

questions.question: Someone writes "The system shall comply with Part 11" in the RS. According to GAMP 5 Appendix D1 §21.3.1.1, what is wrong with this wording?

options.A: Nothing; this kind of regulatory citation is the best way to write an RS, and reviewers can check directly against the regulation
options.B: General, unverifiable statements of this kind should not be written in; the RS should define the functions users need to manage risk
options.C: Only Category 3 systems may be written this way, while Category 4 and 5 systems must cite the regulation clause by clause
options.D: The supplier's ISO certificate should replace such statements, and the regulated company need not define any functional requirements separately

questions.explanation: §21.3.1.1 states that an RS should not contain general, unverifiable requirements such as "Part 11 compliant" or "GMP-compliant", and should instead define the functions users need to manage risk. The view that such regulatory citations are the best way to write an RS is exactly the practice the original text argues against.

questions.question: A project uses an iterative Agile management approach. According to GAMP 5 Appendix D1 §21.3.1, how should requirements (the RS) be regarded?

options.A: Agile needs no requirements of any form; the team simply develops, and the requirements documents are assembled afterward at validation
options.B: All requirements must be finalized and approved before the first sprint begins, with no adjustments allowed afterward
options.C: Backlog items are regarded as the RS, organized using predefined categories such as epics and user stories
options.D: The backlog is only internal reference information for the team and not part of the RS, so traditional requirements documents must be written separately for validation

questions.explanation: §21.3.1 states that in iterative Agile, backlog items are regarded as the RS, using predefined categories (epics, features, user stories, etc.) to structure the requirements. The statement that all requirements must be finalized before the first sprint is the opposite of the iterative, progressive approach.

questions.question: A system is hosted by a service provider, and its configuration and design specifications (CS/DS) are usually produced by the service provider. According to GAMP 5 Appendix D3 §23.3.2, how should the regulated company handle this?

options.A: No specification documents are needed at all, because the service provider is responsible for all system configuration, design, and maintenance
options.B: It must rewrite the entire CS/DS itself and may not use any related documents produced by the service provider
options.C: The regulated company writes and maintains the CS/DS entirely, and the service provider need not supply any related information or documents
options.D: Leverage the service provider's output, supplement the specifications where necessary, and provide oversight through a quality agreement

questions.explanation: §23.3.2 states that the CS/DS of a hosted system is usually produced and maintained by the service provider; the regulated company should leverage it and, where necessary, produce supplementary specifications for configuration that supports the intended business processes, and provide oversight through a quality agreement. Requiring the company to rewrite the entire CS/DS is not what the original text requires.

questions.question: According to GAMP 5 Appendix D5 §25.1.1, what is the Guide's attitude toward unscripted testing techniques such as exploratory testing?

options.A: They are encouraged, to broaden test coverage and improve defect discovery, but must be documented and can be included in overall verification
options.B: They are expressly prohibited; all testing must follow step-by-step scripted test protocols, otherwise it is invalid
options.C: They are permitted, but being informal testing they need no documented record and cannot be part of verification
options.D: They may be used only by the supplier in its development environment, and the regulated company may not use any unscripted testing during validation

questions.explanation: §25.1.1 states that testing should not be limited to detailed scripted protocols; unscripted techniques such as exploratory testing are encouraged, but they must be documented and can then be included in overall verification. The statement that informal testing needs no documented record contradicts "must be documented".

questions.question: The supplier has performed extensive and effective testing during its development life cycle, and it has been confirmed sufficient to show that the system meets the supplier's specifications. According to GAMP 5 Appendix D5 §25.8.1, how can the regulated company's verification be adjusted?

options.A: All testing can be omitted entirely, with the supplier's report replacing any verification activity by the regulated company
options.B: It can be limited to testing a subset of the requirements; the more extensive and effective the supplier testing, the less testing is needed
options.C: It must still repeat all of the supplier's test items, and the supplier's test results may not be used as any reference
options.D: Only IQ needs to be performed; OQ and PQ may not be performed by the user at all because the supplier has already tested

questions.explanation: §25.8.1 states that the more extensive and effective the supplier testing, the less testing the regulated company needs to do; if it is confirmed to be sufficient, the regulated company's verification can be limited to a subset of requirements testing (Figure 25.3). The statement that all testing can be omitted goes beyond the original text.

questions.question: According to EU GMP Annex 11 as cited in GAMP 5 Appendix D6 §26.1, what is required of the system description for a critical system?

options.A: A network topology diagram drawn once at go-live is enough, with no further updating or maintenance of its content and version
options.B: Only Category 5 custom systems need one; standard and configured systems need not prepare one at all
options.C: The supplier's product manual can replace it, with no need to describe the regulated company's own data flows and interfaces
options.D: It must be up to date, covering physical and logical layout, data flows, interfaces, prerequisites, and security measures

questions.explanation: §26.1 cites Annex 11: critical systems should have an up-to-date system description covering physical and logical layout, data flows and interfaces, software and hardware prerequisites, and security measures. The statement that it is drawn once at go-live and never updated violates the "up-to-date" requirement.

questions.question: According to GAMP 5 Appendix D8 §28.3.1, using Scrum as an example, what are the characteristics of a sprint?

options.A: Time-boxed and designed as a short cycle (for example 2 to 4 weeks), with unfinished backlog items returned to the backlog
options.B: It lasts about 6 months, with no scope adjustments during it, and all unfinished items must be forcibly completed in the next sprint
options.C: The cycle is not fixed, and the quality unit decides the length and scope of the next sprint at the end of each sprint
options.D: Every sprint is fixed at 12 weeks, and unfinished items are treated as cancelled and must be resubmitted as a new project request

questions.explanation: §28.3.1 states that a sprint is time-boxed and designed as a short cycle, for example 2 to 4 weeks, with unfinished backlog items returned to the backlog. The statement that it lasts about 6 months does not fit the description of a "short cycle".

questions.question: According to GAMP 5 Appendix D9 §29.2, which of the following software falls outside the scope of "tools" in that appendix and requires risk-based computerized system validation?

options.A: A tool used to mask or anonymize test data for use in system testing
options.B: A testing tool that supports automated and regression testing and stores test results
options.C: Software used to migrate or convert GxP records
options.D: An IT service management tool used to receive and catalog service requests, incidents, and changes

questions.explanation: §29.2 gives examples: software used to migrate or convert GxP records requires computerized system validation, while a tool used to mask data for use as system test data does not. A testing tool supporting automated and regression testing also does not itself need validation, but its records must be retained and protected.

questions.question: According to GAMP 5 Appendix D10 §30.2.2, how should a Layer 2 solution that is a private/permissioned network be regarded?

options.A: It may not be used in any GxP process, because a private network offers none of the benefits of decentralization
options.B: It can be regarded as a shared computing environment, requiring appropriate change control and governance, similar to relying on a cloud computing provider
options.C: Every network node must be treated as a Category 5 custom application, with full software development validation completed individually
options.D: No governance or change control is needed, because the underlying Layer 1 already provides sufficient security and decentralization

questions.explanation: §30.2.2 states that a private/permissioned Layer 2 can be regarded as a shared computing environment, requiring appropriate change control and governance, similar to relying on a cloud computing provider, while still benefiting from the security and decentralization of Layer 1. The statement that no governance or change control is needed does not match the original text.

questions.question: A company's ML subsystem uses online learning, continuously updating model parameters during operation. According to GAMP 5 Appendix D11 §31.3.5.1, what control is required for this kind of dynamic ML?

options.A: Exactly the same as static ML; standard data validation and change management processes are sufficient
options.B: No monitoring is needed after go-live, because the model learns by itself and keeps improving its own performance
options.C: It needs to be assessed only once at the first go-live of the model, with no periodic review or monitoring afterward
options.D: Additional controls are needed, such as continuous and rigorous performance evaluation; in all cases, periodic review and monitoring of model performance are also needed

questions.explanation: §31.3.5.1 states that for static ML with supervised, validated data, standard change management is enough; dynamic ML or unsupervised data needs additional controls such as continuous performance evaluation, and in all cases periodic review and monitoring are needed to detect drift, overfitting, and so on. The statement that it is exactly the same as static ML treats dynamic as static.

questions.question: Several users successively report repeated crashes of the same system, and IT finds a common root cause. According to GAMP 5 Appendix O4 §36.1, which concept does this root cause correspond to?

options.A: An incident, because it is the service disruption event itself that affected multiple users
options.B: A deviation, because any system issue must first be classified as a deviation before further handling
options.C: A problem: a problem is the root cause of one or more incidents
options.D: A change request, because once a root cause is found it must be corrected immediately by change, with no separate classification

questions.explanation: §36.1 defines an incident as an unplanned interruption or reduction in quality of a service, and a problem as the root cause of one or more incidents; problems are causes and incidents are effects. The statement that it should be classified as an incident reverses cause and effect.

questions.question: Someone argues that daily backups can serve directly as long-term record archiving. According to GAMP 5 Appendix O9 §41.1, what is the relationship between backup and archive?

options.A: Backup supports DR, while archive supports readable access during the retention period; backup should not be used as an archive
options.B: The two have the same function; as long as backups are frequent enough, they can replace an archive and meet access needs during the retention period
options.C: The main purpose of an archive is disaster recovery, while the main purpose of a backup is long-term retention and maintaining readability
options.D: A backup copies only data and does not include configuration or software; an archive includes configuration, software, and system settings

questions.explanation: §41.1 states that backup supports DR and archive supports access to records in a readable and meaningful form during the retention period, and a backup should not be used as an archive. The statement that a backup copies only data and does not include configuration or software does not match the original text, in which backup covers data, records, configuration, and software.

questions.question: According to GAMP 5 Appendix O10 §42.1, what are the respective focuses of business continuity (BC) and disaster recovery (DR)?

options.A: BC focuses on restoring computerized systems and data to a point in time (RPO); DR focuses on keeping the business running during a disaster
options.B: BC keeps the business running during a disaster; DR restores systems and data to a point in time (RPO) within an agreed time (RTO)
options.C: Both are limited to computerized system failure scenarios and do not include loss of a service provider or loss of access to the site
options.D: RPO is the maximum time needed for system restoration; RTO is the maximum extent of acceptable data loss; both fall within BC

questions.explanation: §42.1 explains that BC focuses on keeping the business running during a disaster, while DR focuses on restoring systems and data to a known point in time (RPO) within an agreed time (RTO). The statement that BC focuses on restoring to a point in time (RPO) swaps the focus of the two; the statement that both are limited to computerized system failure contradicts the scenarios listed in the original text, such as loss of a service provider or site.

questions.question: According to GAMP 5 Appendix O5 §37.1, how should the scope and depth of a CAPA plan be determined?

options.A: Always use the most thorough investigation and corrective and preventive actions, regardless of the degree of impact the deviation or nonconformance has on quality
options.B: Only deviations that delay product release need CAPA; other deviations need only be recorded in the system log
options.C: The supplier decides on its own according to its internal processes, and the regulated company need not take part in or review the CAPA content
options.D: It should be commensurate with the risk the deviation or nonconformance poses to patient safety, product quality, and data integrity

questions.explanation: §37.1 states that the scope and depth of a CAPA plan should be commensurate with the risk that the related deviation or nonconformance poses to patient safety, product quality, and data integrity. The statement that the most thorough investigation is always used violates the principle of commensurate risk.

questions.question: A company is considering cloud storage to hold archived GxP records. According to GAMP 5 Appendix O13 §45.1, how is this practice viewed?

options.A: Not permitted; archived records may be kept only on physical media within the company's own premises
options.B: Cloud storage may be used only when the records are non-GxP data; GxP records may not use it
options.C: Acceptable, but archived records must still be retrievable at any time for business or regulatory purposes
options.D: Acceptable, and because cloud storage is used, the backup and restore requirements are also deemed fulfilled

questions.explanation: §45.1 states that using cloud storage to hold archived records is acceptable and that archived records should be retrievable at any time; archive and backup should not be confused. The statement that cloud storage also fulfills backup and restore requirements confuses archive with backup.

questions.question: A laboratory analyst uses a spreadsheet to calculate the mean and standard deviation of 10 test values; the results are recorded and the electronic file is not retained. According to GAMP 5 Appendix S3 §48.2.1, how should this disposable spreadsheet be documented?

options.A: Full computerized system validation must be completed first, with functionality reconfirmed before each use
options.B: As with a calculator that has no print function, record the input values and results and sign to confirm
options.C: The electronic file must be kept permanently, with a full audit trail enabled to record every cell modification
options.D: No record is needed at all, because it is only a temporary calculation and the results will not be used in any GxP decision

questions.explanation: §48.2.1 states that a disposable spreadsheet is used like a handheld calculator and the electronic file is not retained; as with a calculator that does not print, the input values and results should be recorded and signed. Requiring permanent retention of the electronic file is the opposite of the "not retained" premise.

questions.question: According to GAMP 5 Appendix S2 §47.4.1, how does review by exception (RBE) treat the electronic production record (EPR)?

options.A: It deletes all data within acceptable ranges and keeps only out-of-range data as the final production record content
options.B: It reviews only a small randomly sampled portion of data, with the rest not checked by any person or system function
options.C: It replaces the entire release procedure, so the product no longer needs any form of personnel review or final disposition decision
options.D: A verified system function filters the data and generates a report containing all critical exceptions, without deleting or altering EPR data

questions.explanation: §47.4.1 states that RBE uses a verified system function to filter data and generate a report containing all critical process exceptions, reducing or eliminating review of data within acceptable ranges, without removing or changing the data in the EPR. The statement that data within acceptable ranges is deleted is the opposite of the original text.

questions.question: According to GAMP 5 Appendix S4 §49.2, how should the regulated company's patch and upgrade management approach generate records and decide on testing?

options.A: Record the version, patch level, and extent of testing; testing can be waived when the release notes show no impact
options.B: Every patch must undergo full regression testing, regardless of whether the release notes indicate any impact
options.C: Patching is a security activity, so no configuration or change records are needed and the extent of testing need not be stated
options.D: Install all patches immediately once a threat is detected, without assessing the impact on the compliance status of regulated systems

questions.explanation: §49.2 requires configuration records showing the version and patch level and change records stating the extent of testing, and notes that the release notes may be used to determine that the application is unaffected, in which case no testing is needed. The statement that all patches are installed immediately once a threat is detected ignores assessment of the compliance status of the regulated system.

questions.question: A company outsources the operation of a GxP computerized system. According to GAMP 5 Appendix S6 §51.5, how should the audit of the outsourced organization be planned?

options.A: Audit only once before signing the contract, with the audit scope limited to regulatory compliance and no other aspects
options.B: After outsourcing, fully adopt the outsourced organization's QMS, with the regulated company no longer needing to perform any audit
options.C: The outsourced organization must be audited initially and periodically afterward, with the audit scope including compliance and financial aspects
options.D: Equipment ownership automatically transfers to the outsourced organization, so the regulated company need not consider equipment ownership

questions.explanation: §51.5 states that the outsourced organization needs to be audited initially and periodically, with scope including compliance and finances; it must also be considered whether equipment ownership transfers and whose QMS is used. The statement that equipment ownership transfers automatically treats the transfer as automatic, which does not match the original text's "must be considered".

questions.question: According to the GAMP 5 glossary (Appendix G2), how is Business Continuity Planning (citing ISO/IEC 27031:2011) defined?

options.A: Documented procedures that guide organizations to respond, recover, resume, and restore to a pre-defined level of operation following disruption
options.B: Documented evidence that the results of an instrument or device, compared with those of a reference or traceable standard, are within specified limits
options.C: A systematic approach to proposing, evaluating, approving, implementing, and reviewing changes, used to manage the change process of a system
options.D: A complete set of records relating to all relevant process information, kept in any physical or electronic format

questions.explanation: §53.2 defines Business Continuity Planning as documented procedures that guide organizations to respond, recover, resume, and restore to a pre-defined level of operation following disruption. The definition showing that instrument results are within specified limits is Calibration, the definition about proposing, evaluating, approving, implementing, and reviewing changes is Change Management, and the definition of a complete set of records relating to all relevant process information is a Batch Record.
